newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call money ends higher, gilt prices steady.
newsitem.headline: Indian call money ends higher, gilt prices steady.

text.p: Reduced supply of funds drove Indian call money rates up to 6.25 percent on Tuesday before they eased to end the day at 5.5 percent, dealers said.
"Rates went up to 6.25 percent at one stage in the morning," said a dealer. "But once banks had covered their positions, rates eased and by afternoon to around 5.5 percent."

Dealers said the supply of funds had reduced as several lenders had invested their funds in treasury bills available on tap with the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) at 4.6 percent per annum. Some funds had also been invested in repo transactions with the RBI, they added.
Call money rates were below one percent most of last week.
Dealers said the low call rates would have induced lenders to invest in on-tap treasury bills and repos, leading to the reduced funds supply this week.
Prices of government securites were steady in moderate trade, dealers said.
"Prices did not fall as expected by some market players," said a dealer. "Normally when call rates firm up, prices of securities fall. Today prices were steady or fell marginally."
